claim: Cathédrale Saint-Apollinaire is open year-round with restricted volunteer-managed hours: Thursday 10:00–12:00, Saturday 8:30–12:00 and 14:00–17:00, Sunday 9:00–11:00.
quote: Thursday from 10am to 12pm, Saturday from 8:30am to 12pm and 2pm to 5pm, and Sunday from 9am to 11am

claim: The Pendentif, a Renaissance funerary monument built in 1548 in the former cathedral cloister for Canon Mistral, is free to visit and was one of France's first listed historic monuments (1840).
quote: Renaissance funerary monument constructed in 1548 within the Cathedral cloisters for Canon Mistral... became one of France's earliest listed monuments in 1840

claim: The Maison des Têtes, at 57 Grande Rue, was built 1528–1532 by Antoine de Dorne and marks the transition from flamboyant Gothic to Renaissance, with sculpted heads of the Winds, Fortune, Time and allegorical figures across its facade.
quote: constructed between 1528 and 1532 by Antoine de Dorne... marks the transition from flamboyant Gothic style to Renaissance style, and owes its name to the numerous heads that ornament its facade

claim: The Maison des Têtes courtyard is free to enter without booking; the building now houses the Pays d'Art et d'Histoire department and guided tours can be booked through it.
quote: visit the courtyard for free... building houses the 'Pays d'Art et d'Histoire' department

claim: The Musée de Valence – Art et Archéologie occupies the former episcopal palace next to the cathedral and is open Wednesday–Sunday 10:00–12:30 and 14:00–18:00 (10:00–18:00 in July–August), closed Mondays, Tuesdays and public holidays.
quote: open Wednesday to Sunday from 10am to 12:30pm and 2pm to 6pm. In July and August, it's open Wednesday to Sunday from 10am to 6pm

claim: Musée de Valence admission is €9 / €7 reduced from 7 March to 21 June 2026 and €6 / €4 from 22 June to 9 October 2026, free for under-18s and on the first Sunday of each month (except July/August).
quote: From March 7 to June 21, 2026: €9 / €7 (reduced). From June 22 to October 9, 2026: €6 / €4 (reduced). Admission is free on the first Sunday of each month

claim: Parc Jouvet, a 7-hectare landscaped garden inaugurated by President Émile Loubet in 1905, sits below the Champ de Mars esplanade and has been a labelled 'Jardin Remarquable' since 2006.
quote: Jouvet Park is a 7-hectare green oasis... Since 2006, Jouvet Park has been designated a 'Remarkable Garden'

claim: The Kiosque Peynet, built 1862 (current iron structure by Eugène Poitoux, 1890), inspired Raymond Peynet's famous 'Amoureux' lovers drawing in 1942 and was classified a historic monument in 1982.
quote: designed by Eugène Poitoux and dates from 1890... inspired Raymond Peynet's celebrated lovers in 1942... classified as a historical monument in 1982

claim: The Champ de Mars is a 3-hectare esplanade (≈300 × 100 m) created in 1773 on an alluvial terrace acting as a balcony over the Rhône, with a panoramic view across to Château de Crussol perched on the Ardèche limestone foothills.
quote: 3 hectares... 300 mètres long by 100 meters wide... le château de Crussol, perché sur les contreforts calcaires du département voisin de l'Ardèche

claim: The Vieux Valence is laced with picturesque 'côtes' — stepped lanes (Saint-Martin, Saint-Estève, Sainte-Ursule, des Chapeliers, de la Voûte) historically used by boatmen and carters to climb from the lower town to the medieval upper city.
quote: montées connecting lower Basse Ville to the elevated old town... Notable côtes include Saint-Martin, Saint-Estève, Sainte-Ursule, des Chapeliers, and de la Voûte

claim: Valence's main military museum is the Musée des Spahis at the Quartier Baquet near the town hall, open only Wednesday mornings 9:00–12:00 (or by appointment), free admission, covering the 1st Spahis Regiment 1830–1991.
quote: tous les mercredis matin de 9h à 12h... Entry is free... regiment's evolution from 1830 through 1991

claim: The boulevards Bancel/Gambetta replaced the demolished 19th-century ramparts and are lined with Haussmann-style Belle Époque buildings, with Eugène Poitoux's monumental fountain (1887) at the corner of boulevards Bancel and Maurice Clerc.
quote: wide promenade traced on the former location of the ramparts and bordered by 'Haussmann-style' buildings... monumental fountain, a work by architect Eugène Poitoux dating from 1887

claim: The Hermitage hillside has signposted walking paths up through the terraced vineyards to the Chapelle Saint-Christophe at the summit, with the 'Sur les Pas de Gambert, en Hermitage' interpretive trail explaining the terroir.
quote: Sur les Pas de Gambert, en Hermitage… an informative track across the hillside… The summit snack… The ascent is not hard… but still makes your calves warm up

claim: The Chapelle Saint-Christophe sits at 329 m elevation above Tain and gives a panoramic view over the Drôme and Rhône valley; a Roman temple to Hercules once stood on the site.
quote: Chapelle Saint-Christophe… 329 metres… built in 1864 on a site believed to have previously housed a Roman temple dedicated to Hercules

claim: From the Taurobole square in central Tain, the walk up to the Saint-Christophe chapel takes about 45 minutes; alternatively you can drive to the Pierre Aiguille belvedere and reach the chapel on foot in 10 minutes.
quote: a simple walk up to the chapel from the Taurobole Square in Tain, taking about 45 minutes… drive to the Pierre Aiguille lookout and walk to the chapel in about 10 minutes

claim: Cité du Chocolat Valrhona in Tain-l'Hermitage is open Mon 10:00–12:00 / 13:00–18:30, Tue–Sat 09:00–12:00 / 13:00–18:30, and Sun/holidays 10:00–12:00 / 13:00–17:30, closed only 1 Jan, 1 May and 25 Dec.
quote: Monday: 10am - 12pm and 1pm - 6:30pm, Tuesday to Saturday: 9am - 12pm and 1pm - 6:30pm, and Sunday and holidays: 10am - 12pm and 1pm - 5:30pm

claim: The Marc Seguin footbridge linking Tain-l'Hermitage to Tournon-sur-Rhône was built 1847–1849 and is the oldest suspension bridge in France still in service, classed as a historic monument in 1985.
quote: Marc Seguin Bridge (Tournon-sur-Rhône/Tain-L'Hermitage, 1849)… oldest suspension bridge in France still in service

claim: Marc Seguin and his brothers built the world's first wire-cable suspension bridge over the Rhône between Tournon and Tain in 1825, predating the current pedestrian span by two decades.
quote: In 1825, Seguin and his four younger brothers built the world's first suspension bridge in which the roadway was suspended from wire cables; it was erected over the Rhône river between Tournon and Tain l'Hermitage

claim: The Château-Musée de Tournon-sur-Rhône is open daily 18 March–1 November 2026, with afternoon-only hours (14:00–18:00) in May and June; full-price ticket €5, reduced €4.
quote: March 18 to November 1, 2026… May 2 to June 30: daily from 2 pm to 6 pm… full price €5, reduced price €4

claim: The Train de l'Ardèche steam train departs from Saint-Jean-de-Muzols just outside Tournon and runs into the Gorges du Doux, with the full-day 'Mastrou' service leaving Tournon at 10:15 and returning at 17:00 between April and late October.
quote: 10:15 am departure from Tournon St Jean by steam train, 11:00 am arrival at Boucieu le Roi… 4:15 pm departure from Boucieu le Roi by steam train for the return journey, ending at 5:00 pm

claim: Paul Jaboulet Aîné's Vineum in Tain offers three tasting formats — by-the-glass with charcuterie/cheese, paired with the chef's dishes, or as a guided educational session — and can be combined with a walk up to the Chapelle de l'Hermitage vineyard.
quote: the pleasure version with wine by the glass accompanied by charcuterie and cheese, the gourmet version with the Chef's dishes, or the educational version during guided tasting sessions

claim: The M. Chapoutier tasting cellar at 18 avenue du Dr Paul Durand in Tain-l'Hermitage is open roughly Mon afternoon–Sat 10:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00 (Sat to 17:00); reservations on +33 4 75 08 97 40.
quote: Monday afternoon to Saturday: 10:00am - 12:00pm / 2:00pm - 6:00pm, with Saturday closing at 5:00pm

claim: The Cave de Tain co-op produces the five northern Rhône crus (Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Péray, Cornas); 45-minute guided visits with a 5-wine tasting cost €15/pp and run May–August daily at 10:30 and 15:30 (French) plus 14:30 in English, by reservation.
quote: 5 crus of the Rhône Valley: Crozes-Hermitage, Hermitage, Saint-Joseph, Saint-Péray and Cornas… Guided visits last approximately 45 minutes plus a tasting of 5 wines, costing 15€ per person

claim: The most highly regarded Saint-Joseph producers — Gonon, Chave, Coursodon and Gripa — are clustered in the village of Mauves on the right bank just south of Tournon, the so-called 'Gang of Mauves'.
quote: Mauves is famous for well-known producers including Gonon, Chave, Coursodon and Gripa—a group known as the 'Gang of Mauves'

claim: Domaine du Colombier in Mercurol (Florent and David Viale) farms 16 ha of Crozes-Hermitage and Hermitage with a sales cellar open April–October daily 09:30–12:30 / 14:30–19:00.
quote: April to October daily 9:30am to 12:30pm and 2:30pm to 7pm… 16 hectares in Crozes-Hermitage and Hermitage

claim: The Château de Crussol and its Ridges loop is a moderate ~4.8 km hike with ~210 m elevation gain, taking roughly 1.5–2 hours.
quote: moderate hike covering 3 miles with an elevation gain of 685 feet, taking about 1.5–2 hours to complete

claim: From the castle car park it is a 20-minute walk to the summit; from the Rhône Crussol Tourist Office, 40 minutes; a 3-hour circuit goes around the entire massif, with sturdy shoes recommended on rocky terrain.
quote: 20-minute walk to the summit from the castle car park; 40-minute walk starting from the Rhône Crussol Tourist Office; a 3-hour circuit trail labeled 'Crussol: a mountain packed with history'

claim: Crussol is exposed and arduous in hot weather — best months are April–June and September–October, water and sun protection essential, with only patchy forest shade.
quote: The climb can be arduous, especially in hot weather, and it's advisable to bring water and a hat to protect yourself from the sun. While the best time to visit is during spring and early autumn months from April to June and September to October

claim: Carbone Zéro at 24 rue Denis Papin, beside Valence's train station, rents both classic and electric bikes and is Accueil Vélo certified — the most convenient ViaRhôna rental in central Valence.
quote: Carbone Zéro - Magasin Cycles La Gare, 24 rue Denis Papin, 26000 Valence... a wide range of electric and classic bicycles along with rental services

claim: Around 130 e-bikes are spread across 35 ViaRhôna partners; daily rental sits at €35–55 and high-season reservation is recommended a month ahead.
quote: 130 electric bikes are distributed among 35 partners along ViaRhôna... daily rates of 35-55 € for quality electric bikes... advisable to reserve your electric bike at least a month in advance during high season

claim: The Tain-l'Hermitage to Valence ViaRhôna stretch is around 19 km of mostly asphalt greenway on stabilized track, an easy half-day ride through Hermitage vineyards and Rhône recreation areas.
quote: signposted linking route on stabilized greenway from Tain-l'Hermitage to La Roche-de-Glun bridge... asphalt greenway between La Roche-de-Glun and the entrance to Valence

claim: Bois des Naix offers a 5 km footpath across 12 hectares of mature trees with a fitness trail, playground, and the Vallée des Fleurs aquatic garden — easy family walking right in the agglomeration.
quote: Bois des Naix (in Valence) — Distance: 5km footpath. Features: '12-hectare green space' with mature trees, Vallée des Fleurs, aquatic plants, fitness trail, and children's playground

claim: Col de Rousset (1,254 m tunnel) has two orientation tables giving 360° views of the climatic boundary between the green Northern Alps and Provence — a panoramic chair lift runs in summer to reach the upper belvedere without hiking.
quote: Two orientation tables allow you to discover a magnificent panorama: one located at the exit of the tunnel on the Diois side, the other at the top of the resort chairlift (accessible in summer and winter by chairlift...)

claim: Col de Tourniol (1,145 m), reached via Barbières, is one of the western entry gates to the Vercors with a quiet road and beautiful viewpoints — under an hour from Valence and a good easy Vercors-edge driving option.
quote: The Col de Tourniol at 1,145m is one of the entry gates to the western side of the Vercors massif, featuring a quiet road with beautiful viewpoints and pleasant, moderately challenging grades

claim: Col de la Bataille (1,313 m) above Léoncel offers a fabulous panorama of the Vercors combes and cliffs and is one of the rare road passes into the south Vercors, around 45 minutes from Valence.
quote: The Col de la Bataille at 1,313 meters altitude is one of the rare road passages allowing access to the South-Vercors... The panorama of the combes and cliffs is fabulous!

claim: Bois des Naix is described as the second-largest urban park in the former Rhône-Alpes region, maintained chemical-free, with 140 animal species and a permanent orienteering course of 20 beacons — bikes, music, and dogs are prohibited.
quote: Bois des Naix is the 2nd largest urban park in the Rhône-Alpes region... 140 animal species, some considered 'remarkable'... permanent orienteering course where you can search for 20 beacons... Bicycles, music, and animals are prohibited

claim: The Suisse de Valence is a soldier-shaped shortbread biscuit created to commemorate the Swiss Guards who accompanied Pope Pius VI's remains after he died in Valence in 1799; about 15 bakeries in the region produce it including Nivon, Patisserie Giraud, Pascalis and Guillet.
quote: Une pâtisserie parfumée, à la fois croquante et moelleuse... Maison Nivon (Valence), Pâtisserie Giraud (Valence), Maison Guillet (Romans-sur-Isère), Maison Pascalis (Bourg-de-Péage)

claim: Maison Nivon, founded in Valence in 1856 by Félix Henry Léon Nivon, makes the canonical Suisse — a crispy shortbread perfumed with orange blossom and studded with candied orange peel — and ships nationally; 250g starts around €8.50.
quote: a shortbread cookie delicately perfumed with orange blossom and adorned with candied orange peel... Founded in 1856 by Félix Henry Léon Nivon in Valence

claim: Ravioles du Dauphiné are tiny square pasta pillows filled with Comté AOC, fresh cheese and herbs; they carry Label Rouge and have held IGP status since 2009, restricted to production between Romans and Saint-Marcellin.
quote: Since 2009, they've possessed Protected Geographic Indication status, requiring production between Romans and Saint-Marcellin in the Dauphiné region... featuring Comté AOC, fresh cheese, or aromatic herbs

claim: La Ravioline at 18 rue Dauphine in central Valence is a market-style bistro built around ravioles, run by chef Alexandre (from Romans) for over a decade, with options ranging from poached ravioles to a ravioline burger and Valrhona-chocolate dessert ravioles.
quote: friendly market eatery in the center of town with fine ravioli dishes for which the house is famous... Chef Alexandre, who was born in Romans, cooks up home-style cuisine

claim: Pogne de Romans is a crown-shaped brioche perfumed with orange blossom dating to the Middle Ages, originally baked communally for Easter and now eaten year-round across the Drôme.
quote: delicately perfumed with orange blossom dates back to the Middle Ages. Originally, for Easter celebrations, housewives would make brioches that they baked together in the communal oven

claim: Maison Pascalis, founded in Bourg-de-Péage in 1892, is the reference producer for Pogne de Romans, having passed the recipe down four generations.
quote: The Pascalis bakery was founded in 1892 by the family's great-grandfather. This bakery makes the famous brioche called Pogne de Romans, for which the company has been renowned for four generations

claim: Picodon AOP is a small, firm raw goat-milk cheese from the Drôme and Ardèche (plus the cantons of Valréas and Barjac), made by 138 producers across the region with around 17,920 goats; the name comes from Provençal 'picaoudou' meaning 'small spicy cheese'.
quote: Picodon is a French goat cheese made from raw, whole milk. The name derives from Provençal 'Picaoudou,' meaning 'small spicy cheese.'... 138 active producers... 17,920 dairy goats

claim: Picodon received its AOP in 1983 and was historically transported from mountain farms down to market towns including Valence; first records of the cheese date to the 14th century around Dieulefit and Valréas.
quote: Since 1983, the Picodon bears the AOP label... The first evidence of this goat's cheese goes back to the 14th century in the Ardeche communes... and the towns of Dieulefit and Valréas in the Drôme

claim: Clairette de Die is the Drôme's natural sparkling white wine made mostly from Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (75% minimum) using the méthode dioise ancestrale — single fermentation continued in bottle without added yeast or sugar — yielding a low-alcohol (7-8%) wine with peach and apricot notes.
quote: made from the Muscat Blanc à Petits Grains (75% minimum) and Clairette (25% maximum)... At 7% or 8% ABV, it contains less alcohol than most sparkling wines... characterized by its peach and apricot flavours

claim: Saint-Péray is a small northern Rhône AOC just west of Valence producing still and sparkling whites from Marsanne (~92%) and Roussanne; sparkling wines account for two-thirds of output, with the first sparkling Saint-Péray made in 1829 by Louis-Alexandre Faure inspired by Champagne.
quote: Saint-Péray is a small appellation for still and sparkling white wines... to the west of the city of Valence... Sparkling wines represent 2/3 of the production... in 1829 he produced the first Saint-Péray sparkling wine

claim: The Saturday market on Place des Clercs runs 7am-2pm year-round with around a hundred stalls of fresh local products, spilling from Place des Clercs to Place de l'Université and Place des Ormeaux at the foot of the cathedral.
quote: Every Saturday, 7 am to 2 pm (year-round)... around a hundred stalls... It stretches from the Place des Clercs to the Place de l'Université and the Place des Ormeaux

claim: Valence has a daily rotating roster of morning food markets across different squares (Place Danton Monday, Place de l'Europe Tuesday, Place de la Paix Wednesday, Place des Clercs Thursday and Saturday, Place Faventines Friday) plus the Place Saint-Jean covered hall Tuesday afternoons 4-7pm.
quote: Place Danton — Monday... Place de l'Europe — Tuesday... Place des Clercs — Thursday... Place des Clercs — Saturday... Place Saint-Jean (market hall) — Tuesday, 4:00-7:00 PM

claim: Valence is building 'Halle Terroir', a new gourmet food hall in a 1234 building (former Jean-Bouin hall) in the basse-ville with one restaurant plus 19 food-only merchants (butcher, charcutier, fishmonger, cheesemonger, greengrocer, wine merchant, roaster, brewer, street-food); opening was targeted for October 2025 but delayed roughly three months by protected martins nesting under the roof.
quote: originally expected to open in October 2025... three-month delay due to martins nesting in the building's roof... a restaurant and 19 merchants, exclusively in food-related trades

claim: Caillette de Chabeuil — a small pork-and-liver patty laced with spinach or Swiss chard, wrapped in caul and baked — sits alongside ravioles and Drôme black truffle as the region's signature savoury specialities and is sold by virtually every local charcutier.
quote: the celebrated ravioles de Romans, the succulent caillette de Chabeuil, and the famous black truffle of the Drôme

claim: Romans-sur-Isère's Musée international de la Chaussure displays 16,500 collector's pieces of footwear spanning 4,000 years inside a former Visitation convent.
quote: 16,500 collector's items from antiquity to the present day, representing 4,000 years of history, are displayed in rotation in the cells once occupied by the Visitation nuns.

claim: Romans-sur-Isère sits about 20 km northeast of Valence, a short hop via the A49.
quote: A few kilometers north of Valence, when heading toward the Vercors, highway A49 takes you to the International Shoe Museum in Romans-sur-Isère.

claim: Marques Avenue Romans groups 80+ outlet boutiques (fashion, shoes, leather) in a renovated former barracks in the city centre, with 30% off year-round and up to 70% off in sale periods.
quote: More than 80 fashion and home boutiques... The stores offer their previous collections at 30% off all year round, and up to 70% off during sales periods.

claim: The Cité de la Raviole at Mère Maury (Romans/Mours-Saint-Eusèbe) offers free interactive exhibits on the ravioles savoir-faire plus free factory-workshop visits with tasting.
quote: Factory visits to the production workshops in Mours-Saint-Eusèbe are offered free of charge with the possibility of tasting.

claim: The Tour de Crest is the tallest medieval keep in France at 52 m, open daily 10am–7pm May to September.
quote: This 52-m high castle tower can be scaled via staircases for great views of Crest and the Drôme River.

claim: Built in the 13th century, the Tour de Crest later served as a state prison from the 17th to mid-19th centuries.
quote: Built in the 13th century for the lords of Crest, it was both a defensive fortress and seigneurial residence. The tower became a prison from the 17th century to the mid 19th century.

claim: Valence to Crest is roughly 30 km and ~29 minutes by car.
quote: The distance between Valence and Crest is 30.2 km... The travel time is 29 minutes

claim: 2026 is the official Année Sévigné at Château de Grignan, marking the 400th anniversary of Madame de Sévigné's birth with a full programme of events including the inaugural 7–8 February weekend and a historical reenactment 30 April–3 May 2026.
quote: 2026 marks the Drôme's celebration of the 400 years since the birth of Madame de Sévigné... From April 30 to May 3, 2026, Grignan travels back in time with a major historical reenactment weekend

claim: Valence to Grignan is about 78–79 km (mostly A7) and roughly 1 hour by car.
quote: The drive from Valence to Grignan covers a distance of 78.8 kilometers, with 51.9 kilometers on the A7 highway... The journey takes approximately 59 minutes by car.

claim: Mirmande is officially classed among Les Plus Beaux Villages de France — a stone hilltop village of ~590 residents overlooking the Rhône valley, revived by cubist André Lhote's summer school.
quote: Mirmande, un des plus beaux villages de France

claim: Valence to Mirmande is about 33 km and ~31 minutes by car.
quote: Distance 33,1 km dureé 31 minutes

claim: The Forêt de Saoû is a 2,500-hectare limestone massif billed as the most beautiful perched syncline in Europe; its high point is Les Trois Becs at 1,589 m.
quote: The Saoû forest... is a limestone massif stretching over 2,500 hectares and home to exceptional biodiversity. It is the most beautiful perched syncline in Europe.

claim: The full Trois Becs loop is around 10 km with ~1,130 m of climb and takes roughly 6 hours; a short version to Mont Veyou only is ~6 km / 3.5 hours / 660 m gain.
quote: the complete circuit of the Trois Becs is approximately 10 km with an elevation gain of 1,130 metres, requiring approximately 6 hours to complete

claim: Sections of the Forêt de Saoû are closed between 15 May and 15 July to protect chamois during calving — partial impact on hikers visiting in early June.
quote: Until July 15, 2026, temporary quiet zones have been established in the Saoû forest to protect chamois during the calving season. Certain sections are closed between 15 May and 15 July.

claim: In early June Provence's lavender fields are still green and not yet visibly in bloom; Drôme provençale lavandin only begins flowering mid- to late June, peaking early to mid-July.
quote: In early June, lavender fields in Provence are not yet in bloom. In May, fields are still green, and the transition to visible bloom happens later in the month.

claim: In Drôme provençale, lavandin flowering starts mid-June in the plain (Grignan, Tricastin) and runs to mid-July in higher sectors like Vinsobres and Roche Saint-Secret.
quote: In Drôme provençale, the flowering of lavandin starts in mid-June in the plain regions like Grignan and Tricastin, continuing until mid-July in the highest sectors such as Vinsobres and Roche Saint-Secret.

claim: Nyons hosts La Maison des Huiles d'Olive et Olives de France with tastings, cooking workshops and a permanent exhibition, open 18 March–23 December 2026.
quote: The House of French Olives and Olive Oils is available from March 18 to December 23, 2026.

claim: Vignolis, the commercial arm of the Nyonsais agricultural cooperative founded in 1923, offers guided mill tours in Nyons.
quote: Vignolis, located in Drôme Provençale on the territory of the Baronnies in Nyons, is the commercial subsidiary of the Cooperative Agricultural Company of Nyonsais, created in 1923

claim: Valence to Nyons is roughly 100 km and about 1 hour by car.
quote: The distance between Valence and Nyons is 100 km by road, taking approximately 1 hour and 1 minute.

claim: The Université du Vin, founded in 1978 and headquartered in the Château de Suze-la-Rousse, runs more than 100 professional and amateur courses on viticulture, oenology and sommellerie.
quote: Each year, the Wine University offers more than a hundred training actions covering all themes and professions, from the vine to the glass through the cellar

claim: The Université du Vin occupies the Château of Suze-la-Rousse, owned by the Drôme regional council.
quote: The Université du Vin, founded in 1978, has its headquarters at the château of Suze-la-Rousse, which is owned by the Drôme regional council.

claim: Le Poët-Laval is a medieval ex-Hospitaller commandery (founded 12th c.) classed Plus Beau Village, set in the Jabron valley about 20 km from Montélimar amid lavender and wheat fields.
quote: Le Poët-Laval, situé dans la Drôme provençale, est un magnifique village médiéval classé parmi les Plus Beaux Villages de France

claim: Valence TGV station sits about 10 km north-east of the city centre in Alixan, with Paris journeys around 2h15 and Lyon around 34 minutes.
quote: The station is about ten kilometres north-east from the town centre, located in Alixan.

claim: A direct TER train links Valence TGV to Valence-Ville in about 8 minutes hourly, with a parallel bus shuttle running roughly every 30 minutes in ~25 minutes.
quote: direct train service departing from Valence TGV and arriving at Valence Ville with services departing hourly, operating every day, taking approximately 8 minutes

claim: Early-June daily highs in Valence climb from about 23 to 27 C (73 to 80 F) with lows around 13 C, and clear skies roughly 54% of the day.
quote: average daily high temperatures increase from 73°F to 80°F during June

claim: June in Valence sees roughly 13 rainy days and about 57 mm of rain over the month, so a weekend visitor should plan for the possibility of a shower.
quote: There are usually 13 days with some rain in Valence in June and the average monthly rainfall is 57mm.

claim: TER trains run roughly 27 times a day between Valence-Ville and Tain-l'Hermitage-Tournon, taking about 10 minutes — easy day-trip access to Hermitage wines.
quote: you can expect to find 27 trains per day running on this popular route

claim: Valence's Libélo bike-share has 68 stations and 431 bikes including e-bikes (60 km range), with the first 30 minutes free and €0.50/30 min thereafter for standard bikes.
quote: 68 stations et 431 vélos, including e-bikes (VAE). Pricing includes 30 minutes free, 0,50€/30 min

claim: The Musée de Valence (art and archaeology, in the former bishops' palace) is open Wednesday to Sunday 10am-12pm and 2-6pm — closed Monday AND Tuesday, with €6 admission.
quote: open Wednesday to Sunday from 10am to 12pm and from 2pm to 6pm

claim: The Q-Park Champ de Mars underground car park (5 Place Championnet) has 842 spaces, is open 24/7, and sits next to the Peynet kiosk, museum, Parc Jouvet, cathedral and SNCF station.
quote: 842 parking spaces ... The parking provides convenient access to Kiosque Peynet, the Museum of Fine Arts, Parc Jouvet, the cathedral, and the SNCF train station.

claim: Champ de Mars parking is free between 12 and 2 pm and during August, with the first half hour also free.
quote: the parking is free between 12 and 2pm and in August, with hourly or daily rates, subscription, and long-term parking options available. Additionally, the first half hour is free

claim: Maison Pic, the Relais & Châteaux hotel attached to Anne-Sophie Pic's three-Michelin-star restaurant, sits on avenue Victor Hugo about a 15-minute walk from the historic centre with 17 rooms and a pool.
quote: La Maison Pic is a luxurious 5-star hotel run by chef Anne-Sophie Pic, located in the heart of the city of Valence on the main avenue Victor Hugo

claim: Across France, smaller shops and many restaurants close one weekday — typically Monday if they open Sundays — so a Sunday-Monday weekend in a town the size of Valence will see noticeably reduced opening.
quote: Shopkeepers often close on a Monday if they are open on a Sunday

claim: Valence to Lyon by road is about 102 km on the (tolled) A7, roughly an hour's drive; Paris to Valence runs via the A6 then A7 corridor.
quote: The distance from Lyon to Valence is 102 kilometers by road, including 90 kilometers on the autoroute, taking approximately 58 minutes.

claim: Champ de Mars sits at the centre of Valence between the train station district, Vieux Valence to the north, Parc Jouvet to the west and Place Aristide Briand to the east, so the historic core is walkable end-to-end.
quote: Champ de Mars is ideally situated in Valence's city center, between the train station district and Place Aristide Briand to the east, the Vieux Valence (old town) neighborhood to the north, Parc Jouvet to the west
